From: Liz Chen <liz.chen@medisolutions.com>

Cc: procurement@medisolutions.com
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify transient cross-region replicas and DPA addendum request

Rafael,

Thanks for taking a look at our security questionnaire. Two quick asks we need clarified before procurement can proceed:

1) For customers that require 'region pinning' (EU-only or APAC-only), can Redwood guarantee that primary inference requests and persisted KV caches remain in-region?

2) We understand transient replicas may be used for cache pre-warming or failover. What is Redwood's maximum expected window for transient cross-region replication (minutes/hours)? Any guarantees on data-at-rest encryption and whether keys remain in the pinned region or are accessible across regions?

3) Please share the current subprocessor roster and any subprocessors in the APAC region. Procurement will need location evidence to map to our vendor risk matrix.

I've attached our questionnaire for reference (MediSolutions_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx). We are open to a limited, timeboxed failover approach, but it must be explicit in the DPA addendum.

Can you route to privacy/legal and confirm timeline for an addendum draft?

Thanks,
Liz Chen
Sr. InfoSec Manager
MediSolutions Inc.
[attachment: MediSolutions_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify transient cross-region replicas and DPA addendum request

Hi Liz — appreciate the clear asks. Quick summary answers here; legal will follow with formal language.

1) Region affinity: We default to routing and storing inference request outputs and KV caches in the customer-selected region (pin). For Dedicated and Private customers we offer a hard pin (no cross-region replication). For hosted customers we provide region affinity with strong controls and the ability to pin an account to a primary region.

2) Transient replicas: for hosted customers we sometimes create short-lived replicas for cache warming and capacity burst. Typical windows are under 30 minutes; in exceptional failover events (e.g., regional outage) this may extend to a capped 120 minutes. All transient replicas are encrypted at rest. By default keys are managed by Redwood KMS, but we can provide a Customer-Managed Key (CMK) option where the key material is bound to a region and not exported.

3) Subprocessors: attaching our current roster. See Redwood_subprocessor_roster_20270405.csv — locations column included. We will highlight APAC subprocessors and provide facility addresses for procurement.

Next steps: marissa, can you start an addendum draft that limits transient failover windows to the 120-minute cap and includes notification requirements to the customer's DPO? Markus, please advise on required indemnities/limitations.

Liz — happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk the legal language. When are you available this week?

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Team — looping in legal as requested. Notes for the addendum draft: 

- Commit to region affinity for account primary storage and long-term caches.
- Allow bounded transient replication for: short-lived cache warming (<=30m default) and emergency failover (<=120m maximum).
- Require: proactive notification to customer SOC/DPO within 15 minutes of initiating a cross-region transfer, detailed audit log entry, and a post-incident report.
- Encryption: support CMK with region-bound key material; specify any operational exceptions where key escrow is needed.
- Subprocessor evidence: provide facility addresses and data flow diagrams for APAC subprocessors.

Markus — please embed the notification timing above and a clause that the customer may require a dedicated key as a condition for tighter guarantees. Rafael/Karthik — I'll prepare a DPA addendum draft v1 and attach it for internal review.

Marissa Cole
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposed operational commitment & notification flow

Liz — thanks for the patience. To be explicit about operational mechanics: 

- Operational commitment: Redwood will configure account-level region affinity. For MediSolutions we propose APAC primary. In normal operation all persisted artifacts (KV caches, routed request logs for >24 hours) will remain in APAC.

- Transient exceptions: Redwood will allow automated short-lived replication for cache warming (<=30m) and an escalated failover path with a documented cap of 120 minutes. Failover will be restricted to designated partner regions only (APAC <-> APAC-edge; APAC <-> EU only in declared emergency) — we will not replicate to arbitrary third regions.

- Key handling: when CMK is enabled, key wrapping/unwrapping remains in-region; KMS operations that need to be proxied across regions will be logged and flagged in the audit trail.

- Notification & approvals: Redwood will send an automated incident-style notification to the customer's DPO and SOC within 15 minutes of initiating cross-region replication and follow with a post-event report within 48 hours. For any planned maintenance that may trigger a transient replica (non-zero probability), Redwood will notify 72h in advance and obtain explicit signoff for the maintenance window.

Links: operational runbook draft -> https://drive.redwood.com/teams/compliance/MediSolutions-residency-draft
DPA addendum template (editable) -> https://app.docusign.com/Redwood/DPA-Addendum-Template

If this aligns, we'll prepare the DPA addendum and the DSAR/audit evidence pack. Rafael — I suggest proposing a 30-min review with their procurement/infosec next week.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Product Manager, Region Controls
Redwood Inference
